# Build It, Teach It {.unnumbered}

> The best way to understand a system is to build a small one, then teach someone else what you built.

## Who this is for

This book is for educators, students and self-learners who want to use the **HandsOnAI** lab to build small AI systems and teach the ideas underneath them.

It assumes you can run Python and follow a command line. It does not assume you have built a RAG pipeline, an agent or a classroom AI policy.

## The lab

**HandsOnAI** is a learning lab, not a production framework. Every module is one model call wrapped in plain Python:

- chat adds a system prompt and a transcript
- RAG adds a search before the call
- agents add tools and a loop
- workflows add folders and review gates
- loops add repetition and a stopping rule
- evaluation adds a judge
- vision and voice add converters at the edges

The package is deliberately small. The point is to make the concept visible, not to hide it behind a framework.

## Two tracks

This book has two tracks that meet:

- **Build:** choose a project, scaffold it, test it, document it and show it.
- **Teach:** turn the project into a lesson, an assessment and a classroom policy.

The project chapters are for students and self-learners. The classroom chapters are for educators. The module chapters serve both.

## What you will build

By the end, you will be able to:

- explain the one-call shape behind chat, RAG, agents, workflows, loops, evaluation, vision and voice
- set up a local, shared or cloud lab for a class
- choose a project that fits the time and the learning objective
- build and review a small project with tests and documentation
- design a lesson, an assessment and a disclosure policy
- keep the learning honest when the model is fluent and wrong

## How to read it

Read Part 1 and Part 2 in order. Then choose a project from Part 3 and use Part 4 to teach it.

Each chapter ends with an AI exploration, a build or classroom task, a summary and a reflection. The appendices collect the module map, the project template and the classroom checklist.
